The compressor research package was designed, fabricated, and acceptance tested by AiResearch Manufacturing Company of Arizona under NASA Contract NAS3-9427.
The compressor wheel has a diameter of 4.25 inches and is an exact 0.514 scale-down of an existing high-efficiency compressor design.
The compressor design conditions at the 6.0 kwe reference power level include a pressure ratio of 1.9, mass flow rate of 0.756 lb/sec, and rotating speed of 36,000 rpm.
The compressor is designed to operate with a XeHe working fluid mixture with an equivalent molecular weight of 83.8.
The predicted design efficiency of the compressor is greater than 80%.
The compressor wheel is made of 403 CRES material and has a maximum blade stress of 25,000 psi at the 36,000 rpm operating speed.
The compressor package uses angular-contact ball bearings with a predicted time-between-overhaul of at least 300 hours.
The compressor package includes static pressure instrumentation at the inlet, impeller, diffuser, and scroll exit, with provisions for adding total pressure and temperature instrumentation.
The compressor package successfully completed acceptance testing up to 120% of the 51,200 rpm design speed.
The compressor package is designed to operate between 25,550 and 66,165 rpm without encountering rigid-body critical speeds.
The compressor package has a design clearance between the wheel shroud and housing of 0.007-0.009 inch.
The compressor package is mounted on resilient mounts with a spring rate of 30,000 lb/in to avoid critical speeds.
The compressor package includes a carbon-face contact seal at the impeller end to accommodate a wide range of back-face pressures.
The compressor research package will be used at the NASA Lewis Research Center for complete component performance evaluation.
The compressor design leveraged an existing high-efficiency design rather than developing a new design, as the existing design was expected to meet the performance requirements.
